verified.exploit_entry_point: The shared engineapi.ContextLoaderFactory: the engine builds it with the policy under evaluation and calls Load with the rule's declared context entries. Hidden tests build the same factory for namespaced Policy / ClusterPolicy and load entries into enginecontext.NewContext with deferred loading disabled, so every fix layer (factory, loader, apicall, executor) is exercised through the product entry point. Cleanup coverage drives cleanup.controller.cleanup, the controller's own context-loading path.
routes: T1: namespaced policy apiCall URLPath with explicit other namespace, dot segments, a namespace-name prefix, an all-namespace list path, and a post-substitution namespace; GET and POST share the guard
T2: namespaced policy service call; executor attaches /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token unless the policy supplies Authorization
T3: namespaced policy ConfigMap context entry with another namespace, and with a template that resolves to empty
T8: namespaced CleanupPolicy whose context target resolves empty; the controller builds the shared loader with a nil policy
verified.project_tests_run: go test ./pkg/engine/apicall ./pkg/engine/context/loaders ./pkg/engine/factories ./pkg/controllers/cleanup -count=1 (pinned, oracle, alt, hardening and every check patch)
verified.not_routes_at_pinned: GlobalContextEntry reads (T10) left out deliberately: sharing is arguably by design and the reader flagged it as a fairness risk. Service URLs that name the API server are not tested directly; the credential-lending invariant is tested at the outbound request instead, so a fix that refuses API-server targets and a fix that stops lending the credential both satisfy the property (the must-keep-working functional test requires genuine external calls to keep working).

traps.shape: the published fix's site: URLPath namespace confinement must survive path shapes (dot segments via normalization, namespace-name prefixes, all-namespace list paths) and be applied after variable substitution; the cluster-scoped Namespace object is refused even when it names the policy's own namespace; coupled must-keep-working: own-namespace namespaced-resource reads, templated targets resolving to the policy namespace, and cluster-scoped policies unrestricted
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the reported example is a single literal path, so a substring or prefix check looks sufficient and cluster-scoped traversal looks like the same feature
traps.realistic_because: published fix site (GHSA-8p9x-46gm-qfx2); the shape and keep-working cases are the reader's T5/T6/T7

traps.shape: the outbound HTTP path silently attaches Kyverno's service-account token whenever the policy supplies no Authorization header; a namespaced policy can name any endpoint, including one that leads back to the cluster
traps.reason_to_dismiss: service calls are meant for external HTTP services and look unrelated to the kube API path guard; the token attachment reads as a convenience
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the credential attachment predates the advisory and is untouched by every published fix commit

traps.shape: a second, typed loader implementation resolves a ConfigMap namespace taken from the policy entry with no comparison to the policy namespace; an empty resolved namespace falls back to 'default' rather than the policy's namespace
traps.reason_to_dismiss: ConfigMaps are typed, non-secret shared configuration and the advisory talks about raw API paths, so the typed lookup looks like a different feature
traps.realistic_because: published fix site (GHSA-cvq5-hhx3-f99p): the second implementation the first advisory fix missed

traps.shape: the cleanup controller builds the shared context loader with a nil policy, so a check keyed on the policy argument silently treats a namespaced CleanupPolicy as cluster-scoped; the controller's own namespace is available on the same line
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the cleanup controller is a separate component, its context only feeds deletion conditions, and it is absent from the admission path the report describes
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the nil-policy call is still present after both published fixes
